messages:
erin: Heads-up — customer X reported 401s + duplicate billing right after we rolled regenerated SDKs from the OpenAPI change that wrapped responses in a top-level `data` object. Happens in Python/TS/Go. Repro steps pasted below. @sam @maria :eyes:

sam: Can you paste the exact error + which SDK versions the user is using? Any stack traces?

support-bot: Ticket #INC-4821 — https://support.internal/ticket/4821 — customer attached logs, says failures started at 2026-03-16T15:12Z after they pulled latest SDKs.

maria: From the customer logs: their app gets a 401 from the first request, then our client retry layer re-sends, the second attempt succeeds but payment processed twice (idempotency header not set due to SDK serialization error). Stack: `TypeError: cannot convert <data object> to Foo` in generated deserializer. Looks like regen changed response schema from `Foo` -> `{ data: Foo }` so generated code expects `data` but our runtime mapping sometimes unwraps wrong.

erin: Oof. Is this a codegen bug (template) or an OpenAPI shape change that we should flag for semver?

maria: It's both. The OpenAPI edit added a wrapper for paginated endpoints and accidentally toggled `nullable`/`required` flags for a handful of endpoints. Codegen regenerated clients with the new shape, but our gateway still returns the legacy shape in some regions for backcompat, so clients hit an unexpected type and throw before setting idempotency header.

sam: Repro I ran locally (quick):
```bash
# using ts-sdk v1.12.0-regenerated (commit a1b2c3)
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer redacted" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/foo/123
# gateway returned: {"id":"123","name":"x"}  <-- legacy
# generated TS client expected: {"data": {"id":"123","name":"x"}}  <-- regenerated
```

sam: When the client receives the legacy shape, the generated deserializer returns null for the `data` field and throws a mapping error. Our client runtime treats that as an error and retries the whole request (default retry policy). Because the first attempt actually succeeded server-side but client threw, payment got re-applied.

eng-oncall: Immediate mitigation: I can toggle the compatibility flag in gateway so it returns the regenerated shape (wrapped) for this customer. That will stop throws. But we should avoid forcing shape changes for all customers.

maria: Longer term fixes: (1) patch codegen templates to accept both shapes (if top-level `data` present unwrap it, else accept legacy), (2) add a defensive deserialization fallback that won't cause the call to be rejected (convert to success + log a warning), (3) add an integration test in CI that runs against a shim-mode gateway that returns both shapes.

sam: I'll open a PR tonight for a minimal compatibility patch in the TS/Python/Go templates: add runtime helper `safeUnwrap(response)` that does `return response.data ?? response` and update generated deserializer to call it. Also add a unit test. Will target quick patch branch `devex/regen-compat`.

erin: Can you also add a short changelog note about this OpenAPI change and mark it as breaking unless `compat` enabled? We need to communicate to customers.

sam: Yep. I'll include migration notes and a rollout plan. ETA PR in ~4h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: For the customer in the ticket, support should offer to pause charges and flip the gateway compat flag while we ship the patch. @support-bot please coordinate.

support-bot: Noted — leaving note on INC-4821 and pinging SOC for billing hold.

eng-oncall: Also adding an emergency e2e in staging that regenerates clients from the current spec and verifies idempotency headers are preserved on success/fail paths. If that fails, block release.

erin: Thanks. Assigning ownership: sam -> codegen patch, maria -> CI test + gateway compatibility plan, eng-oncall -> immediate gateway toggle for customer. I'll follow up with the customer and legal on the billing hold. :white_check_mark:
